title: The death penalty (CCC 2267)
hookLine: the Catechism's paragraph 2267 was rewritten to call the death penalty inadmissible

lines: A MARK, SO NO ONE KILLS HIM.
cards: A few verses after Abel's death in Genesis, Cain, the killer, is afraid: whoever finds him, he says, will kill him. Then something unexpected.
In the Douay-Rheims: "And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him." The killer walks away guilty, sent out, and protected.
That small mark sits behind a paragraph in the Catechism of the Catholic Church, number 2267, which Pope Francis approved in new words. Today's word is its subject: the death penalty.

teach.h: THE OLD WORDING: A DOOR LEFT AJAR.
teach.b: First, the older wording. The Catechism used to say that the Church's traditional teaching did not rule out the death penalty, if it was the only way to protect people's lives from an unjust aggressor.
Drawing on John Paul the Second's gospel of life, it added that cases where that is truly necessary are very rare, if not practically nonexistent. A door left open, but only a crack.

The revised paragraph says the death penalty is inadmissible, because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person, and that the Church works with determination for its abolition worldwide.
Inadmissible: not allowed in, not something the Church can accept. Third, the reasons it gives.

teach.h: DIGNITY ISN'T LOST, EVEN AFTER CRIME.
teach.b: A growing awareness that a person's dignity is not lost, even after very serious crimes. A new understanding of what punishment by the state is for.
And ways of detaining dangerous people that protect the public without closing off the guilty person's chance to change.
John Paul the Second, in yesterday's letter, read Cain's mark the same way: not even a murderer loses his dignity.
The Church presents the change as a development of its teaching in the light of the gospel, and Catholic writers have discussed how it fits with what came before. Fourth, the people involved.

teach.h: I WAS IN PRISON, AND YOU CAME TO ME.
teach.b: Jesus in Matthew names among the works that matter, in the Douay-Rheims: "I was in prison, and you came to me." And the Church also keeps close the families of victims, whose grief is real and deserves care.
Both are held in the same hands.

how: Catholics act on this teaching through prison ministry, visits and letters to people on death row, support for victims' families, and advocacy for the abolition of the death penalty, and bishops' conferences in several countries speak publicly on it.

o: the state putting a convicted person to death
being cut off from the Church for good
a life sentence with no chance of parole

games.q: the death penalty — tap the pairs.

s: the Catechism still treats the death penalty as acceptable when a state chooses it
the revised paragraph 2267 calls it inadmissible.
God protects Cain after the murder in Genesis
the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him.
the Church also keeps close the families of victims, whose grief is real.

games.q: a man has done something terrible. he is locked away and the public is safe. what does the revised Catechism say about putting him to death?
o: it's allowed whenever a court decides.
it's inadmissible: his dignity is not lost.
games.why: paragraph 2267 now calls the death penalty inadmissible, an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person, and the Church works for its abolition.

practice: Bring to mind a prison cell you've never seen, a narrow bed, a small window or none, a person waiting; you don't need to know their crime or decide anything about it, just let them be a person.
Then widen the circle: the guards who work there, the chaplain who visits, the families of the people who were harmed, still grieving.
If you pray, hold them all before God together; if you don't, hold them in mind without sorting them.

wordCard.voice: The death penalty. Which the Catechism now calls inadmissible, an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person, even a guilty one. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: inadmissible. Even Cain was given a mark of protection. Go gently.
